# R352 — stock `--long` comparison and controller boundary

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only review of the pristine upstream v0.14.3 `bench.sh`/`tools/strata_bench.py`, current workflow guidance, the v182 registry, prior R338/R342–R345 and R347 reports, and Main's supervisor source packet. No source edit, test/build/import, GPU/service/process/reset operation, or Git change was made. The only new artifact is this report. The excluded `prefill-gemm-only-contract-root-v1/record.json` was not read.

## Decision

The stock comparison is well-defined as three serial fresh HTTP long-prompt requests per arm with the unchanged upstream client, but the label `32K` is a target label. Main's known actual length 32,049 is a successful roughly-32K sample and is below 32,768. The strict `>=32768` adoption rule in the workflow and supervisor is an additional local gate, not a property the stock client can meet reliably. Keep actual counts and outcomes; don't alter prompts or retry them to force a threshold while claiming the pristine stock workload.

For a valid across-arm comparison, use the same pinned upstream client revision and invocation (`--long --runs 3`, no `--clients`, same API mode) against each arm's own dedicated loopback server, with one client at a time and identical server/model/context/environment settings except the candidate variable. Preserve stock suite order and compare the same 32K suite position. For multiple arms, alternate arm order across independently closed/restarted campaign blocks if feasible; stock `bench.sh` itself offers no randomization or counterbalancing. Record per request actual `prompt_tokens`, `read_tokens`, `reused_tokens`, generated count, engine timing/rate source, failures, and arm/order/lifetime identity. Summarize per-arm medians and ranges from the three samples; do not call the inputs exactly paired because the client tags differ by invocation.

The stock client's 24-token `max_tokens` is an output cap for each fresh prompt, not a 24-token sustained decode interval. Generated text can terminate before 24. Keep this workload primarily interpreted as long prefill and first-token behavior; report actual generated counts and per-row engine decode metrics only as short continuation observations. Don't infer a sustained 32K-context decode rate or use the displayed cap as generated work. Independent GEN measurements remain a separate workload: they may diagnose engine phases but must not be pooled, substituted, or ranked in the stock HTTP result or its medians.

## Input length, reuse, and order

The pristine client estimates tokens-per-word from two small calibration requests, constructs `prompt_for(32768, run)`, and sends three fresh prompts with unique run tags. It has no tokenizer feedback loop or actual-length retry. The real usage count is authoritative. At 32,049, the row remains a valid observed roughly-32K fresh-prompt result for descriptive comparison; it does not satisfy a separately declared 32,768 minimum. Do not drop it from the record or relabel its measured count.

“Fresh” describes the request content/session, not a cold engine. Each test suite executes warm-up/calibration, short chat, 4K, 16K, agent, then optional 32K in one client invocation. R345 source audit establishes that with the prepared zero prompt-cache configuration each independent request starts at resume 0 and prior conversation checkpoints are not retained, while the same model, engine, GPU allocations/workers, verifier graph, expert-cache allocation and potentially OS mapped-file residency persist. The agent row has its own within-session reuse semantics; it is not the 32K row. Record observed reuse for every 32K request and the effective cache/checkpoint settings. Never infer 32K reuse from agent cache-hit values or equate process warm state with prompt KV reuse.

Runs within one arm share an ordered persistent server and are therefore not cold independent starts. Across-arm timing comparisons should match suite position and retain uninterrupted server identity/lifetime and preceding suite sequence. A server restart, config difference, cache-setting difference, or insertion of another benchmark before 32K changes the comparison condition and must be recorded. The stock client is single-client in the proposed command (no `--clients`), so requests in the suite are sequential.

## Supervisor audit

The Main controller is an observer/owner around the pristine CLI: it pins pristine `bench.sh`, `strata_bench.py`, Python, server/config/binary and related source identities; invokes `bench.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:<port> --long --runs 3 --out ...`; and requires the upstream result to state `runs=3`, `long=true`, `started_server=false`, contain a non-skipped 32K row with three successful requests and no client errors. It preserves each actual prompt count and nullable generated/read/reused counts and engine metrics; it marks independent GEN outside the stock performance calculation. The campaign also owns one persistent server, checks it remains alive while the stock client runs, assesses idle state after the client, performs normal owned shutdown, and requires the observed normal QUIT/engine exit path. These controls support isolating the HTTP stock result from independent GEN observations.

The review found one material interpretation mismatch: `check_results` retains actual counts correctly, but `performance_eligible` additionally requires all three observed prompt lengths `>=32768`. The stock source does not promise that, and the known 32,049 example demonstrates the gate can reject a completed stock row solely because calibration undershot its target. Therefore `passed/complete` may represent a correctly completed campaign while `performance_eligible=false` means “fails Main's local strict floor,” not “stock benchmark failed” and not “no usable roughly-32K observation.” Preserve this distinction in result summaries. Requiring all three above target can bias adoption toward accidental calibration overshoot and make stock comparison eligibility non-reproducible across otherwise identical arms.

The current Git bench/results artifact was read as corroboration: its three 32K requests each observed 32,049 prompt tokens, zero reused, and 24 generated tokens; engine prompt rates were 403.9, 400.5 and 399.3 tok/s (median 400.5). The row is explicitly present and all requests succeeded. This supports the interpretation above, not a new measurement by this audit. Its short decode numbers (8.7–9.1 tok/s) cover only those 24 generated tokens and remain unsuitable as sustained decode evidence.

The supervisor checks the official client invocation and client params, and pins source identity; it does not independently inspect each outgoing HTTP body's `max_tokens` or assert event-by-event suite ordering. Those are inherited from the pinned pristine source. The source defines long prompts with `LONG_MAX_TOKENS=24` and suite order as above. Thus identify these as source-derived settings, rather than claiming a separate wire capture. It keeps per-request actual counts and does not synthesize rates; engine metric completeness requires engine-sourced prompt/decode rates. This is an appropriate barrier against mixing client-fallback rates or custom GEN timings into stock results.

Reuse values are validated as nonnegative when present, but controller logic does not itself require zero reuse or reject missing reuse counts; the result assessment preserves them. For a strict fresh-prompt interpretation, missing reuse remains an evidence limitation, while nonzero reuse should be disclosed and considered in interpretation. The current known campaign has normal QUIT evidence and successful requests; debug COPY0/1 is explicitly not performance eligible, consistent with the separate quiet-only gate.

## Smallest workflow correction

`docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.ja.md` currently says to exclude every trial below 32,768 tokens. This is stronger than the upstream's “about 32,768” target and conflicts with the same document's instruction to use pristine generated inputs without replacement. Minimal wording correction:

> `--long` adds the upstream row targeted at about 32,768 input tokens. Keep every successful request and report its actual count. Describe it by observed length (for example, 32,049 tokens); reserve “at least 32,768” for trials that actually meet that explicit threshold. A local threshold may define a separate eligibility subset, but does not turn lower successful stock trials into failed measurements. Record reuse and output counts per request.

Then change the controller's strict-floor gate to a clearly named optional analysis classification, or define stock eligibility as three successful rows with valid recorded observed counts and required engine metrics, while separately reporting how many meet any chosen actual-length floor. Do not silently substitute a custom GEN input to satisfy it. This is a proposal only; no documentation or controller change was made.

## Prior-report coverage and sources

This audit intentionally does not repeat the calibration mechanism and known 4K/16K deltas (R344), decoded rate/fallback semantics or 24-cap conclusions (R338/R342/R343), broad lifetime/reuse details (R345), or phase-cache admission requirements (R347). Those reports and their v182 registry entries were read to avoid duplicating their findings. Registry v182 lists 872 completed research items and includes the relevant upstream reports. No runtime evidence was generated here.

Sources: pristine upstream at HEAD `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`, `bench.sh`, `tools/strata_bench.py` (`LONG_MAX_TOKENS`, `Suite.run_prompt`, `Suite.run`, result serialization); workflow `docs/MEASUREMENT_WORKFLOW.ja.md`; Main controller packet `main-upstream-benchsh-supervisor-source-v3/supervisor.py.txt`; current Git artifact `bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-first-gpu/upstream/results.json` and `upstream/README.md.json`; registry `report-registry-v182.json`; prior reports R338, R342, R343, R344, R345, R347 under `research-20261009`.
